svg.title: ARM break-even advice: two concurrent positions
svg.desc: Illustrative sample: two long positions on one bid price/time chart. Order 1 blue, order 2 purple. Human actions are square chips and filled cells, order-server actions are outlined cells; the action table runs in one time sequence with order 1 on the left and order 2 on the right.
svg.text: A1 · You go long: fill 1.10000, stop 1.09800
within ~2 s. No notice is sent.
B1 · You go long: fill 1.10050, stop 1.09950
Effect: its own 1R = 0.00100. Its bar 0 is
10:15–10:30; armed on its own, no notice.
Same PRE email as order 1, one item each.
so it is dropped (no basis held).
A2 · You tighten the stop to 1.09900
Effect: real risk 0.5R, but the test keeps
1.09800 until a bar end confirms: the
B2 · You follow the advice: stop 1.10050
Effect: risk 0, at target. No state change
until the 11:00 bar end; next PRE silent.
PRE bar 2: at target, no basis: no item.
held for the verification re-read. Not in
A3 · You follow the advice: stop 1.10000
Effect: risk 0, at target. Released at the
PRE bar 4: at target, no basis: no item.
Released: COMPLETE again, held for the
T+60 s: part-0 email lists only order 1,
as awaiting the broker's final bar.*
Same time on both sides = one shared notice for the route: one email, one item per order.
Each order keeps its own state, stop basis and cursor; they share the bid series, the notice
per bar end and its verification re-read. (A netting account would merge them: not shown.)
* Current behaviour flagged in review (see the note).
